title: Version 0.140.0 - Migration and Super App Features
description: Version 0.140.0 released on June 15, 2025, adding /usage token-activity views, /import feature to migrate from Claude Code, codex delete session command, and unified interface improvements. Major 'Super App' update introduced computer use capabilities, image generation, 90+ plugins, multi-terminal support, and SSH functionality.

community_feedback.quote: Codex is rapidly degrading — please take this seriously
Claude Code migration becomes easier: /import lowers friction for users moving setup
War on X & Reddit: Claude Code vs Codex - Claude acknowledging performance drops while Codex gains ground

title: Cursor 1.0 - Production-Ready Release
description: Cursor 1.0 released on June 4, 2025, with BugBot for automatic code review, background agent access for everyone, memories feature, one-click MCP setup, Jupyter notebook support, and enhanced chat output. This marks Cursor's transition from beta to production-ready AI code editor.

community_feedback.quote: The market for AI-assisted development is exploding and token costs are plummeting all the time. It makes sense for them to subsidise usage to capture market
Cursor 1.0 rocks! - User feedback praising smoother experience in agent mode with Sonnet 4, improved context handling without headaches
Cursor 1.0 is their BEST update yet... (Agents, BugBot...)
Discussion about monthly AI costs for larger projects, focus on production use cases

title: Copilot Coding Agent Public Preview
description: GitHub Copilot Coding Agent entered public preview on May 19, 2025, with rollout continuing through June 2025. AI agent can implement tasks/issues, runs in background with GitHub Actions, handles feature additions, bug fixes, test extensions, and refactoring. VS Code June release included MCP support and improved chat/agent workflows.

community_feedback.quote: GitHub's new Copilot coding agent is absolutely incredible - blows me away despite using it for months
Introducing GitHub Copilot agent mode - reliably working for edit unlike Roo which misses things
GitHub Copilot Agent looks promising – much, much smarter, feels like human coworker
Agent looks much more capable than it did 2 months ago
